_README: A MEASURED scene. Every number here is something you put a tape measure
or a caliper on; nothing in it is detected. This is the first-hour path:
automatic perception can come later, and the kit never needs it — it
needs an observation.
UNITS AND CONVENTIONS, because getting one of these wrong is the whole
of the 8.47 mm class of mistake:
* metres and radians. Always. There are no millimetres in this file.
* 'base' is the robot's base frame: +x forward, +y the robot's LEFT,
+z up, origin on the torso platform. It is where the kit's inverse
kinematics reports, so it is the root of every transform.
* 'p' is the object's CENTRE, not its bottom and not a corner. A 50 mm
cube standing on a table whose top is at z = 0.010 has p[2] = 0.035.
* 'size' is the full extent along the object's OWN three axes, in the
order (length, width, height) of that object's frame. A yawed box has
the same size and a different 'yaw_rad'.
* 'yaw_rad' rotates the object about base +z. Use 'quat_xyzw' instead
if you have a full orientation.
* a 'container' also takes 'interior': the usable INNER extent, which
is what a placement is checked against. If you leave it out the kit
marks it ESTIMATED and refuses to place into it, because the walls
then are not where anybody said they are.
* 'frame_id' names the frame the pose was measured in. Objects measured
against a table you calibrated go in that frame; the transform goes
in 'frames'. A frame with 'max_age_s' expires, and everything
measured in it then refuses rather than returning a plausible number.
The 'table' entry is a SURFACE, which is what a Place lands on and what
a Lift is checked as having left.
